Table 3: Nutrients available per 10,000 kJ, by Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage(a) – Estimates
Apparent Consumption of Selected Foodstuffs, 2023–24: Geospatial Dietary Indicators
(a) See the Glossary in the Apparent Consumption of Selected Foodstuffs Methodology, 2023–24 for definitions of terms used in this publication.

(b) A lower Index of Disadvantage quintile (e.g. the first quintile) indicates relatively greater disadvantage and a lack of advantage in general. A higher Index of Disadvantage (e.g. the fifth quintile) indicates a relative lack of disadvantage and greater advantage in general. See Socio–Economic Indexes for Areas (Index of Relative Socio-Economic Disadvantage), Australia, 2021 (abs.gov.au).

(c) Alcoholic beverages as a food group are not available from source data. However, alcohol as a macronutrient may be present in food items (e.g. desserts). See the Explanatory Notes in the Apparent Consumption of Selected Foodstuffs Methodology, 2023–24 for more information.
